newsitem.title: USA: "The Birdcage" wins top honors at Guild Awards.
newsitem.headline: "The Birdcage" wins top honors at Guild Awards.

text.p: Zany comedy film "The Birdcage" won one of the top honours at the Screen Actors Guild Awards on Saturday in a surprise victory over other movies that are considered likely favourites to win an Oscar.

While the Screen Actors Guild does not hand out a "best picture" award, it honoured "The Birdcage" for best ensemble performance in a motion picture, over such films as "The English Patient" and "Shine", both Academy Award nominees.
"The Birdcage", which was released early last year was not nominated for an Academy Award for best picture.

"For the first time in my life, I was totally speechless," one of the film's stars, Nathan Lane, said after the ceremony. "You could have knocked all of us over with a feather. We were in a state of shock."

Screen Actors Guild Awards, which are based on the votes of the 78,000 members of the actors' union, are seen as an endorsement of actors by their peers, and often as a precursor of likely winners at the Academy Awards, which will be presented next month.

Small, independent films were also among the big winners, with Frances McDormand honoured as best actress in a motion picture for her role as a police detective in the offbeat murder film "Fargo"; and Geoffrey Rush winning the best actor award for "Shine", the story of brilliant young pianist destroyed by mental illness.
Both McDormand and Rush are up for Academy Awards.
McDormand told reporters backstage she was gratified by the award for a role she had originally resisted taking because it was so close to home.

"I'm from the Midwest and I've waddled all my life. I wanted to do something the farthest from that, not something that was so close to my existence. But then when we started working on it I realised it was one of the best gifts I'd ever been given," she said.

Other actors honoured included Cuba Gooding Jr., as best supporting actor in a motion picture for his role in "Jerry Maguire"; and Lauren Bacall as best supporting actress for "The Mirror Has Two Faces".

In the television category, NBC took most of the top honours, with the cast of "Seinfeld" winning for best ensemble performance in a television comedy and the cast of "ER" winning for ensemble performance in a television drama.

"Seinfeld" star Julia Louis-Dreyfus was honoured as best female actress in a television comedy, and John Lithgow won the best actor award in a television comedy for his role in "3rd Rock From The Sun".
For television drama series, Gillian Anderson won the best actress for Fox network's "The X-Files"; and Dennis Franz, star of ABC's "NYPD Blue", won best actor.
